title: TransportEnvelope
description: The six WebSocket frame shapes exchanged between the laptop (server) and the phone (client); see docs/camera-sync-design.md Sec 4.2 and Sec 4.4, docs/steps/step-20-brief.md (query/answer) and contracts/README.md 'Transport envelope'. The reserved type 'location' (phone -> laptop, defined in a later step) and any other unrecognised 'type' are valid JSON that a receiver logs and ignores -- they are deliberately out of scope for this schema, which only documents the shapes the laptop and phone actually exchange today.

t1.description: Laptop send time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.
Echoed laptop send time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.

t2.description: Phone receive time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.

t3.description: Phone send time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.

health.description: Phone -> laptop. One report of the feedback manager's stale-drop ring (10 one-second buckets of {received, staleDropped}); a rising rate is the trigger for the docs/camera-sync-design.md Sec 3.4 automatic fallback. Advisory only: the laptop's health monitor still steps rungs and flips to the local detector without it, and a report older than 3 s (after clock conversion) is ignored, so a dead signal can never drive a switch.

t_phone_ms.description: When the phone produced this report, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds in the PHONE clock (the laptop converts before judging freshness).

window_ms.description: Width of the whole ring in milliseconds (10 one-second buckets = 10000).

received.description: Events the feedback manager received inside the window.

stale_dropped.description: Of those, the ones dropped for arriving past their TTL (Sec 4.4).

stale_drop_rate.description: stale_dropped / received over the complete buckets; 0 when received is 0. At or above 0.2 over at least 2 complete buckets the laptop flips to the local detector.

complete_buckets.description: How many of the ring's one-second buckets are fully elapsed. Fewer than 2 makes the rate meaningless, and the laptop ignores the report.

phone_frame.description: One rectilinear JPEG from the phone's front camera, captured when the query was asked. Mirroring is off, so image-left is the wearer's left.

jpeg_b64.description: Standard base64 of the JPEG bytes (<= ~2 MB decoded).

hfov_deg.description: Horizontal field of view of the image as sent, degrees.

query.description: Phone -> laptop. A spoken question about the surroundings ('Hey Cane, is there a bathroom around?'). The laptop answers with exactly one 'answer' frame carrying the same query_id; a newer query supersedes an older one still in flight.

kind.description: find: look for 'target' all around. describe_around: summarise the 360 view. describe_front: describe the phone frame (X4 crops optional). ask: any other question, answered in a sentence from every view (and web search when the laptop has it).

target.description: What to find ('bathroom'); required for kind 'find', null otherwise.

utterance.description: The recognised words after the wake word, verbatim.

t_phone_ms.description: When the phone sent the query, PHONE-clock Unix-epoch ms.

answer.description: Laptop -> phone. The one reply to a 'query'. The phone turns bearing_deg into its own direction words; subject and detail are short noun phrases, never directions.

subject.description: What was found ('restroom sign'). Required when status is 'found'.

bearing_deg.description: Torso-relative, same convention as AwarenessEvent.bearing_deg (0 ahead, negative left). Only with status 'found'.

detail.description: Extra context ('past the elevators'), or the whole description when status is 'described'.

latency_ms.description: Laptop-side time from receiving the query to sending this answer.

diag.description: Phone -> laptop. One line of the phone's black-box recorder (what the mic heard, wake-word and intent decisions, what was spoken, link changes, mic level). Advisory and write-only: the laptop appends it to logs/phone-YYYYMMDD.jsonl. Text and numbers only, never audio.

data.text: hey cane is there a bathroom

speak.description: Phone -> laptop. 'Say this in the natural voice': the laptop synthesizes 'text' (ElevenLabs) and replies with exactly one 'voice' frame carrying the same speak_id. Answers and prompts only; hazards are always spoken on the phone.

examples.text: To your right, restroom sign, past the elevators.

voice.description: Laptop -> phone. The audio for one 'speak'. status 'unavailable' (no key, timeout, API error) carries no audio: the phone speaks with its own voice instead.
